title: Medicine - Doris White
writingTask: Using the information in the case notes, write a letter to Mrs Lucy Walters, a Community Nurse, requesting for wound dressing. Address the letter to Mrs Lucy Walters, Newtown Nurse Clinic, 10 Stillwater St, Newtown.
caseNotes: Doris White is 64 years old.
Her date of birth is 1 April 1955.
She lives at 5 Woods St, Stillwater, Newtown city.
She lives alone with her cat and is independent using a frame for mobility.
She is on the social service registry for laundry and cleaning assistance, and has good mental health.
Her past medical history includes type 2 diabetes.
She has chronic renal failure and is on regular haemodialysis.
She has ischaemic heart disease and hypertension.
She has peripheral vascular disease and an area of hyperpigmented skin.
Her medications include aspirin 75mg once daily, atorvastatin 40mg once daily, insulin 50 units twice daily and a beta blocker 5mg twice daily.
She is also on linezolid 600mg, nitroglycerin 4mg PND, calcium 300mg twice daily and multivitamins 2 tablets.
On 25/03/2019 she was admitted to hospital with a neglected traumatic leg injury after slipping in the bathroom.
She was treated with analgesics (paracetamol), antibiotics (amoxicillin) and topical pressure therapy.
On 10/04/2019 the wound remained unhealed, so surgical debridement was performed; her Ankle Brachial Index was 60.
On 17/04/2019 there was no improvement, so a skin graft with flap was performed under general anaesthesia.
By 25/04/2019 the graft was healing 40%, with epithelium growth, and the wound was being treated with hyperbaric oxygen; her ABI was 70.
On 03/05/2019 the graft was healing 50%, and negative pressure dressings were used.
By 18/05/2019 the graft was healing 70%, with an ABI of 70, and discharge was planned.
A list of her medications is to be attached.
Her blood pressure is well controlled and stable; it was last checked last month and should be monitored.
candidateLetter:
Mrs Lucy Walters
Newtown Nurse Clinic
10 Stillwater St
Newtown

18 May 2019 Her blood pressure has been well controlled.

Dear Mrs Walters,
Re: Ms Doris White, DOB: 1 April 1955 Her blood pressure was last checked last month.

I am writing to request your ongoing nursing care for Ms Doris White, who is being discharged today following a skin graft. Her blood pressure remains stable today.

Ms White was admitted on 25 March 2019 with a traumatic leg injury after slipping in the bathroom. Initial paracetamol, amoxicillin and topical pressure therapy did not achieve healing. As surgical debridement brought no improvement, a skin graft with a flap was performed. With hyperbaric oxygen therapy and negative pressure dressings, the graft is now 70% healed, and her ankle-brachial index has improved from 60 to 70.

Ms White has type two diabetes mellitus, chronic renal failure requiring haemodialysis, ischaemic heart disease, hypertension and peripheral vascular disease. Her medications are aspirin, 75 mg daily; atorvastatin, 40 mg daily; insulin, 50 units twice daily and a beta blocker, 5 mg twice daily. She also takes linezolid, 600 mg; multivitamins, two tablets; nitroglycerin, 4 mg and calcium, 300 mg twice daily. Please find enclosed her medication list. She lives alone, mobilises independently with a frame and receives social service assistance with laundry and cleaning.

I would be grateful if you could provide wound dressing for Ms White's graft.

Should there be any queries, kindly do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely, Please continue to monitor her blood pressure.

Doctor
